log.defender:
Here are some resources that explain how browsers and HTTP clients resolve URLs with userinfo components:

1. **URL Standard - User Information**: This document specifies that userinfo (username:password@) is part of the authority component, but the host is what actually gets resolved for network connections. You can read more about it [here](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-representation).

2. **MDN Web Docs - URL**: The URL API parses userinfo components, but the hostname property returns only the domain portion, which is what browsers connect to. More details can be found [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL).

3. **RFC 3986 - Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax**: This specification defines that the host component follows the '@' character in the authority part, and this is what network clients use for resolution. You can access it [here](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986).

These resources should help clarify how URLs with userinfo components are resolved. If you have any further questions or need additional assistance, feel free to ask!
